full_details: Before the house was up you went down in your shirt and cloak. The close smelled of last night's ash. Every door in Great St Helen's was dressed: green birch, fennel, St John's wort, white lilies in a pot on a step, and the little lamp over the Ansells' door still burning against the daylight. You stood under your own lintel a quarter of an hour. Nobody else was up but the sparrows. You were in by six. You did not go south of Cornhill. At nine you rehearsed entrances, and a bill in the house said French Comedy, with no sum. Before noon you counted twenty shillings twice. Mistress Ansell wrote a receipt in her late husband's law-hand. The quarter's candles had come to more than the quarter's bread, and she had never had a lodger of whom that was true. Upstairs, after the rent, the coffer was twenty-five pounds exactly. You entered eight shillings and twelve with no remark, and you set sixty shillings apart in canvas for Thursday. At dinner the loaf looked smaller than winter's. Verbeke said memory makes bread bigger. Alse, cutting it four ways, said cutting does not. You played in the afternoon. You did not tell Kemp. Evening prayer was short, and the glass was not turned.
one_sentence: You stood under the dressed lintel, paid twenty shillings counted twice, and played in the afternoon.
title: Twenty shillings, twice
